newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle off $1 at $67, slow - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle off $1 at $67, slow - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow Thursday, with light sales at $67.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from Wednesday and down $2.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 5,000 head of slaughter steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas, which brought the week to date figure close to 76,000, they said.
No sales were reported in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.
Fed cattle prices this week were pressured by lower beef prices following big cattle slaughter last week, they said.
Slaughter this week was lighter, with 130,000 head estimated Thursday, which brought the week to date number to 522,000, down 2.1 percent from last week's pace of 533,000, USDA statistics showed.
Uncertainty over Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report also weighed on fed cattle prices, market sources said.

The report was expected to show on-feed numbers as of May 1 at 109.6 percent of year-ago levels, according to average pre-report analyst estimates. April feedlot placement estimates averaged 113.9 percent and April marketings averaged 101.0 percent of a year ago.
